tasks.text: 1.6 P-A -- flush the pending campaign envelope before the document is discarded (closes residual (1) in the 2026-08-21 note above). Add the discard-time flush to `src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts` and install/uninstall its listeners in `src/stores/campaign/campaignPersistenceWiring.ts`, beside the existing subscription pair (`installCampaignPersistenceWiring` / `uninstallCampaignPersistenceWiring`, `:39-73`). Measured today: `markDirtyAction` (`:797-820`) only arms a `setTimeout` at `AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 2000` (`:42`), and neither file contains `beforeunload`, `pagehide`, `visibilitychange`, `sendBeacon` or `keepalive` -- zero grep hits at this snapshot -- so up to 2s of mutations are discarded on hard reload or close and task 1.3's head validation then refetch-replaces the localStorage copy of the un-PUT work. **Triggers:** `pagehide`, and `visibilitychange` when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`. Do NOT add `beforeunload`: it fires nowhere `pagehide` does not, and registering it disables bfcache in some engines -- a regression in a fix whose whole purpose is not losing state. **Mechanism:** one `fetch(..., { method: 'PUT', keepalive: true })` at the existing `/api/campaigns/[id]` route with the existing `{ envelope, baseVersion }` body built by `buildSerializedCampaign`, i.e. the same write `putLiveCampaign` (`:456`) performs. `navigator.sendBeacon` is POST-only and that route 405s anything but GET/PUT/DELETE (`src/pages/api/campaigns/[id].ts:125-300`), so a beacon would require a new POST surface for no gain. **The mechanism's own hard limit (RE-1):** browsers cap a `keepalive` request body at 64 KiB summed with in-flight keepalive bytes, and a body over the cap fails as a network error -- which, because this flush never reads its response, would be a silent failure inside the fix for a silent failure. Re-measured on the local dev DB this session (`data/mekstation.db`, `campaigns.payload`, 9 rows): 3310 to 20819 bytes, median 8213, so the largest persisted envelope today is 31.8% of the budget and the mechanism is viable now. It is not safe by construction: 60% of that largest body is `recentlyAppliedOutcomes` (12392 bytes), and `unitCombatStates`, `dailyBattleAudit`, `salvageReports`, `gmInterventionEvents`, `timeCascadeEvents` and `processedBattleIds` are all unbounded in campaign length or roster size. **Therefore measure before firing:** serialize the `{ envelope, baseVersion }` body, and when it exceeds the cap do NOT fire -- record a TYPED diagnostic on the store (the named skip reason `envelope-over-keepalive-cap`, not a cleared flag and not a swallowed error) so an over-cap discard is observable rather than silent. Growing past the cap is then a reported condition with an owner, not a regression nobody sees. **Bounded, at-most-once per discard, never an acknowledgement:** clear the armed timer first (`clearAutoSaveTimer`, `:209`) so the discard path and the timer cannot both write; fire one request; never retry; never queue follow-up work; never read the response -- therefore do NOT clear `dirty`, do NOT advance `baseVersion`, and do NOT call `applySavedRecord`. An acknowledged revision cannot be lost or overwritten this way: the server's `baseVersion` compare-and-swap decides the outcome (`src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:126-131`) and the next load re-validates the cache against the head per task 1.3. **Skip** when not dirty, and when `isCoopCampaign` (`:268`) is true -- the same exemption `markDirtyAction` already applies, because a second writer there is residual (2) above, not a rescued mutation. **FAILING TEST FIRST** in a new `src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignPersistenceCrashWindow.test.ts`: mark dirty, dispatch `pagehide` in jsdom WITHOUT advancing timers, and assert exactly one keepalive `PUT` carrying the CURRENT in-memory envelope and the current `baseVersion`. Red today because no listener exists. Sibling rows: the hidden-transition trigger; at-most-once across a `pagehide` immediately followed by `visibilitychange`; no request when clean; no request for a co-op campaign; the armed timer does not also fire afterwards; and `dirty`/`baseVersion` unchanged by the flush. **Over-cap row (required):** an envelope serializing past the 64 KiB keepalive cap issues NO request and leaves the typed skip diagnostic naming `envelope-over-keepalive-cap`, asserted positively rather than by absence alone. Regression cover: `src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignCommandAutoSave.test.ts`, `src/stores/campaign/__tests__/useCampaignPersistenceStore.test.ts`, `src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignPersistenceWiring.test.ts`. **ACCEPTANCE:** `npm run typecheck`; `npm run lint`; `npx jest src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignPersistenceCrashWindow.test.ts src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignCommandAutoSave.test.ts src/stores/campaign/__tests__/useCampaignPersistenceStore.test.ts src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignPersistenceWiring.test.ts`; `npx openspec validate --all --strict`. NON-CLAIMS: no journal, no command pipeline, no flag flip, no change to the PUT route or its CAS. The flush is best-effort -- a browser that discards the document without firing either event still loses the window; so does a browser that FIRES the event, accepts the `keepalive` request and then declines to dispatch it because the document is leaving via a NAVIGATION rather than a close (measured 2026-09-15 on Chromium 143.0.7499.4, headless and headed alike: `about:blank` navigation 0 landed / 15, same-origin navigation 1 / 2, tab close 11 / 11, reproduced by a 17-byte product-independent `pagehide` probe at 0 / 3 navigation and 3 / 3 close -- `openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion/evidence/r2-client-discard-flush-diagnosis-20260915.json`); and a keepalive request whose response is never read is not evidence it committed. The requirement obliges the client to ISSUE the write, not to guarantee it lands, and the product is conformant on every path measured; the residual is that on this Chromium a user who navigates away still loses up to 2 s of mutations, while tab close, window close and in-app SPA routing are covered. Residual (2), the co-op dual-writer PUT 409 storm, is untouched. This task does NOT satisfy task 6.2a's pre-command durability step: it fires at discard, not when the contract market is generated.

6.1 P0b -- journal-private source envelope, full source baseline, contract-only replay. Add an OPTIONAL journal-private field to `ICampaignJournalEnvelope` in `src/lib/campaign/sync/JournalCampaignEventStore.ts`, a sibling of `campaignEvent`, and leave `envelopeOf` returning `stored.payload.campaignEvent` unchanged. **The field MUST be optional**: `src/lib/campaign/sync/hostCampaignEventJournal.ts:150-153` constructs `ICampaignJournalEnvelope` with all three fields explicit, so a required field stops that co-op host path compiling and turns it into a second construction site that must invent a value. **Collapse the two narrowing sites to one (required by the spec delta, do NOT skip):** grant projection narrows inline today at `src/lib/campaign/delivery/projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:252` (`const event = stored.payload.campaignEvent;`) and never calls `envelopeOf`; replace that line with `const event = envelopeOf(stored);`, adding `envelopeOf` to the value import that file already takes from `JournalCampaignEventStore` at `:62` (no new dependency edge, and that module imports nothing from `delivery/`, so no cycle), so `envelopeOf` is the sole narrowing in fact as well as in the SHALL. Without this sub-step the new requirement is violated on the day it ships and task 6.3's falsification row is vacuous for the grant leak row. Put the private type, its conditional constructor (absent, never `{}` and never an enumerable `undefined`), and the contract-only replay fold in a new `src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts`. Capture the baseline under the P0a prepared transaction (`SQLiteEventJournalWriter.appendPreparedWithExtension`, on main at 79c789e2a): exact persisted `SerializedCampaign` body, source row `version`, source body digest, and root public journal revision. Replay starts from `sourceRecord.body`, not from the compact genesis snapshot, which carries empty contracts and no market (`src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignSourceGenesis.ts`). Borrowed-handle campaign write with CAS plus a durable `sourceReplayFence` that rejects a later generic whole-envelope overwrite goes in `src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts` beside the existing `baseVersion` CAS. Private/public identity mismatch or an unsupported replay schema blocks or rebuilds; no silent compact fallback. Source snapshot/cache version, original command receipt revision, and current journal revision stay three distinct numbers. NON-CLAIMS: no producer, no flag flip, no HTTP surface change.

6.2 P1 -- source `acceptContractOffer` producer, after 6.1 only. This task lands as two ordered prefixes, **6.2a market durability** then **6.2b acceptance routing** (D13); neither is separable from the other's tests, so they share this checkbox and 6.2 is not done until both hold. **6.2a -- the stored offer is durable before the command names it.** Per D13 the market is already persisted in the `SerializedCampaign` body (`src/lib/campaign/persistence/serializeCampaign.ts:194`, read back at `:264`) but only via the debounced PUT, so a command submitted inside that window names an offer 6.1's captured baseline does not hold. **The offer read is the source record body read under the command's OWN prepared transaction (RE-3)** -- the same read task 6.1 records as `ICampaignSourceBaseline.sourceRecordBody` -- NOT a previously-stored private baseline. That distinction is load-bearing: `ICampaignSourceBaseline` has no `contractMarket` field (its four fields are `sourceRecordBody`, `sourceRowVersion`, `sourceBodyDigest`, `rootPublicRevision`), the market is obtained by parsing that body and rehydrating it (surfaced as `ICampaignSourceContractProjection.baselineMarket`), and `replayCampaignSourceContracts` throws `CampaignSourcePrivateReplayError('no-private-payload')` when the stream carries no prior private row -- which is exactly the state of every campaign that has never accepted a contract. Reading the offer from a STORED private baseline would therefore deadlock the FIRST acceptance on every campaign. No private-payload shape change is needed for 6.2a: the P0b envelope already parses `sourceRecordBody` and rehydrates the market. Server half in `src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignCommandPipeline.ts`: look the `contractId` up in that transaction-read market and, when it is absent, refuse with a typed reason DISTINCT from every rules refusal (insufficient standing, already accepted), never falling back to a caller-supplied contract body. Client half in `src/pages/gameplay/campaigns/[id]/contract-market.tsx` (`handleAccept`, `:69-77`; the market is generated in the effect at `:45-53`): obtain an acknowledged save before submitting, using the store's existing `saveCampaign` action (`src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:787` `saveCampaignAction`, which clears the armed timer and delegates to `performSave`, `:549`) -- task 1.6's discard-time flush does NOT cover this, it fires at discard rather than at market generation. Failing test first: in `src/lib/campaign/authority/__tests__/campaignCommandPipeline.test.ts`, submit an AcceptContract naming a `contractId` absent from the market in the transaction-read source body and assert the typed not-durable refusal and that no event is appended; red today because the pipeline reads no source market at all. Sibling row: the FIRST acceptance on a campaign with no prior private row succeeds, proving the read is the transaction-read source body and not a stored private baseline. **6.2b -- exactly one acceptance writer.** `acceptContractOffer` (`src/stores/campaign/campaignCommandActions.ts:454-493`) writes `ICampaign.missions` and rewrites `contractMarket` client-side, while `CAMPAIGN_EVENT_REDUCERS.ContractAccepted` (`src/lib/campaign/sync/applyCampaignEvent.ts:91-97`) writes only the compact `ICampaignAuthoritativeState.contracts` (`src/types/campaign/CampaignSync.ts:66-73`) -- two state trees with no function connecting them. The spec delta records this as an obligation, not a tolerated divergence, and 6.2b owns it: on the committed path the source record's mission and reduced market come from 6.1's contract-only replay fold applied to the SAME commit that produced the compact ledger entry, and the client SHALL NOT also apply locally; on the refused path (including `campaign-not-on-journal-authority`) nothing is committed and today's single client-side write stands. Failing test first: a pipeline row asserting a committed acceptance yields the compact ledger entry AND the source record's mission and reduced market from one commit, plus a `src/stores/campaign/__tests__/campaignCommandActions.test.ts` row asserting the client does not also apply on the committed path and still applies exactly once on the refusal path. Route the toolbar path in `src/stores/campaign/campaignCommandActions.ts` (today a browser-store mutation) through the source command pipeline in `src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignCommandPipeline.ts` and the existing active-seat route `src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts`, whose authorization gate is unchanged. Command identity is `sha256(canonical({ campaignId, authenticatedActorId, kind: 'AcceptContract', contractId }))` with `expectedRevision` excluded; duplicate receipt lookup happens BEFORE the offer read. The compact `name` and `employerFactionId` on the emitted `ContractAccepted` are server-derived from the stored offer, with `employerFactionId` the exact opaque `IContract.employerId` -- no alias table, no case folding. The full contract and the remaining market go to 6.1's private envelope only. Acknowledgement returns the original receipt revision plus the current public head. **Recorded dependency (RE-4):** that acknowledgement carries journal-side numbers plus a compact `ICampaignAuthoritativeState` with no missions, while the client's compare-and-swap token is the `SerializedCampaign` row `version` -- which 6.2b's source-side record write advances behind the client's back, so the next unrelated client auto-save PUT conflicts or meets 6.1's `sourceReplayFence`, and the client's rendered `ICampaign` has no post-acknowledgement refresh path (the cache requirement covers LOAD-time validation only). That mapping is the admission brief's unresolved P-C and is owned by task 6.4 below; 6.2 SHALL NOT be treated as closing it. The `/commands` response, guest/room-code hydration, and the co-op mirror keep their current compact shapes. Browser-generated offer persistence is NOT assumed; a `generateAtBContracts` call in the contract-market page is not evidence the server stored the offer. This source command SHALL NOT be replaced by a co-op archival API. NON-CLAIMS: no full private HTTP readback (still blocked), no flag flip, no cutover, no CAMP witness.

6.3 Boundary proofs for 6.1 and 6.2. Red-first at the real SQLite reopen boundary in `src/lib/campaign/sync/__tests__/JournalCampaignEventStore.test.ts`: commit an accepted contract carrying full detail, reopen, and assert the source recovers it from the private field while `envelopeOf` yields only the compact fact. Leak rows in `src/lib/campaign/delivery/__tests__/projectCampaignStreamForGrant.test.ts` and `src/lib/campaign/coop/__tests__/roomCodeGuestHydration.test.ts` assert no employer, target, payment terms, salvage rights, morale, AtB type, or market offer reaches a campaign-scope delivery item or a recomposed hydration snapshot, with the GM all-scopes grant as a same-shape control rather than a wider one. A legacy row proves a pre-private envelope canonicalizes to identical bytes and an identical state digest. Producer rows live in `src/lib/campaign/authority/__tests__/campaignCommandPipeline.test.ts`. Falsify each boundary 1:1: deleting the `envelopeOf` narrowing must turn the leak rows red while the compact control stays green. This falsification is only valid AFTER 6.1 routes `projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:252` through `envelopeOf` -- run it and confirm the grant leak row actually goes red, because with the inline narrowing still in place that row stays green and the proof is vacuous. A third row asserts the accepted residual honestly: `projectedEventIdentity` on a delivered item still equals the stored `eventDigest` computed over the whole payload, so the test pins the commitment as EXPECTED rather than pretending the private bytes leave no trace on the wire.

6.4 Bridge the two compare-and-swap counters after a committed acceptance (the admission brief's P-C; owner of the dependency 6.2 records). Two independent optimistic-concurrency tokens exist today with no defined mapping: the `SerializedCampaign` row `version`/`baseVersion` the whole-envelope PUT uses (`src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:103-158`, client side `src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts`), and the journal stream revision `expectedRevision` the command route uses (`src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignCommandPipeline.ts`; response shape in `src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts`). Before 6.2b they never met, because the source never wrote the campaign row on a client's behalf. After 6.2b it does, so a committed acceptance must leave the client able to (a) continue auto-saving without a spurious conflict or a `sourceReplayFence` refusal, and (b) render the accepted mission without waiting for a reload. Define the mapping and the post-acknowledgement refresh, stating explicitly which of the two numbers the client cache is keyed by -- task 1.3 keys it by `(instanceId, revision)` and this task SHALL say which revision that is. NON-CLAIMS: not sized here; no flag flip; no widening of the `/commands` response is assumed to be the answer -- a refetch of the source record is an admissible answer and may be the smaller one. This task exists so the dependency has an owner in the package rather than only in a session artefact; it is NOT a licence for 6.2 to ship the mismatch unrecorded.
